protected_conclusions.statement: LDVB is approximate; MCMC remains the reference when posterior tails or interval accuracy are central.
The Q--DESN 500-target sensitivity is development-linked evidence rather than an untouched confirmation experiment.
MQ--DESN reduces crossings more consistently than it improves predictive score.
All reported multiquantile winner and runner-up marginal intervals overlap.
The descriptive GloFAS score leader remains undercovered, with particularly poor upper-quantile frequency for MQ--DESN exAL.
Q--DESN does not dominate PriceFM in aggregate and its comparison varies by region and fold.
Calibrated MTI evidence is restricted to a fixed eight-distribution panel and is not a distribution-free theorem.
MTI width is not uniformly smaller than Young--Mathew, especially near the sample-range boundary.
The pharmaceutical splits overlap, partition choice matters, and physical units for the derived response remain unresolved.
The proposed endpoint regression and dynamic models have no matched implementation, simulation study, or application.
